# **Pull Request: EKS GitOps Migration** 

## **Summary**
**EKS GitOps Migration and Hardening**

## **Description**
This PR migrates the **Modular Learning Hub** to a production-ready **AWS EKS** architecture using a robust **GitOps (ArgoCD)** workflow. The infrastructure has been modularized and hardened with a comprehensive **DevSecOps suite** in the CI/CD pipeline.

---

### **Architecture & Infrastructure (Terraform)**
- **Three-Tier Modular Design:** Refactor of networking, security, compute, database, and gitops into standalone modules.
- **Cost Optimization:** EKS nodes configured with **Spot Instances** for maximum efficiency.
- **High Availability:** Transitioned to **Multi-AZ RDS** for production databases.
- **KMS Encryption:** Configured AWS KMS for EKS secrets encryption at rest.

###  **DevSecOps Security Suite**
Integrated the following automated scanning tools into the CI pipeline:
- **Trivy:** Image vulnerability scanning (CVEs).
- **Checkov:** IaC security and compliance scanning.
- **Kube-linter:** Managed manifest security and best practices Audit.
- **Gitleaks:** Secret detection and prevention.
- **Hadolint:** Dockerfile best-practice enforcement.

### **GitOps & Pipeline Logic**
- **ArgoCD Automation:** Syncs `k8s/` manifests automatically to the EKS cluster.
- **Environment Management:** Dynamic configuration for `staging` and `production` via separate `.tfvars`.
- **Quality Gate:** Standardized code formatting across all services via **Black**.

---

## **Checklist**
- [x] Terraform modules validated and planned.
- [x] All microservices scan clean (Trivy/Hadolint).
- [x] No sensitive secrets committed (Gitleaks verified).
- [x] Environment-specific variables injected securely.

author: samhagman
body:
## Situation
Harnessd v2 shipped with a single-model architecture — Claude for all roles. After the form-builder run, post-run QA found integration bugs that evaluators rubber-stamped because the same model built and verified the work.

## Complication
The evaluator needs to be a genuinely adversarial reviewer — a different model with different blind spots. Additionally, the form-builder run revealed that evaluators were hallucinating evidence (claiming to see Set-Cookie headers that didn't exist), builders were adding graceful fallbacks instead of making things work correctly, and the Codex CLI sandbox was blocking Playwright browser testing.

## Resolution
This PR adds multi-model adversarial evaluation and hardens every prompt based on real findings from the auth-identity harness run (14+ hours, 10 packets, 50+ evaluator rounds).

## Summary

### New capabilities
- **CodexCliBackend** — spawns `codex exec --json`, parses JSONL output into AgentMessage stream. GPT-5.4 with xhigh reasoning for evaluator sessions
- **BackendFactory** — per-role backend selection (`--codex-roles evaluator,qa_agent`). Claude builds, Codex evaluates
- **Tool gates** — typecheck + test gates between builder and evaluator. Failed gates skip the evaluator entirely (saves tokens)
- **QA agent phase** — holistic e2e browser testing after all packets complete
- **Round 2 planner** — targeted fix packets based on QA findings
- **Plan review phase** — Codex reviews Claude's plan before operator approval (caught 4 major issues on first real run)

### Prompt hardening (from real run findings)
- **E2E state verification protocol** — evaluators must observe actual behavior at every step, not infer from code. "Did I observe this or infer it?" anti-hallucination rule
- **No graceful fallbacks** — builders must make things work one way (the specified way), not add degraded-mode alternatives
- **Evaluator can run commands** — start dev server, curl endpoints, run tests. Not just read-only code review
- **Pre-submission quality** — builders run `/simplify` + `/code-review` before claiming done
- **Playwright --isolated awareness** — all prompts know new browser windows are fresh contexts with no cookies/state

### Infrastructure fixes
- `workspaceDir` persisted in RunState, restored on resume (gates were running in wrong directory)
- `roleBackends` + `codexModel` restored from config.json on resume
- Codex sandbox: no `--sandbox` flag for workspace-write roles (Playwright needs ~/Library/Caches access)
- Codex CLI: prompt as positional argument (was `--prompt` flag — broke every eval session)
- All max limits raised to 10 (negotiation rounds, fix loops, retries, QA rounds, plan review)

## Test plan
- [x] 225/225 tests passing
- [x] 0 TypeScript errors
- [x] Codex evaluator verified working (curl + Playwright) via manual test
- [x] Real harness run (auth-identity) exercising all new features
- [x] Plan review caught 4 major issues on first use
- [x] Tool gates correctly blocked evaluator when typecheck/tests failed

body:
## Overview
This PR implements the ability to add member dependants to committees, allowing dependants (children, relatives) to be assigned committee positions alongside regular members and spouses.

## Feature Highlights
- ✅ Add dependants to committees with minimal database changes
- ✅ Automatic dependant loading when selecting a member
- ✅ Intelligent relation inference (e.g., if partner is "Son", dependant is "Daughter-in-law")
- ✅ Visual selection UI with highlighted cards
- ✅ Separate duplicate tracking (member, spouse, and each dependant are independent)
- ✅ API support with contextual remarks field
- ✅ Graceful handling of deleted dependants

## Database Schema

### Committee Table
**Existing columns utilized:**
- `memberid` (int) - Parent member ID
- `isspouse` (tinyint) - 0 for member/dependant, 1 for spouse (unchanged)
- `dependantid` (int NULL) - **Key field**: When NOT NULL, indicates this is a dependant

**Design Decision:** 
- Keep `isspouse` as 0 or 1 only (unchanged from original design)
- Use `dependantid IS NOT NULL` to identify dependant records
- No foreign key constraint (allows graceful handling of deleted dependants)
- Unique combination: `memberid + isspouse + dependantid`

## Backend Changes

### 1. Models Updated

#### `common/models/basemodels/Committee.php`
- Added `dependantid` property and validation rules

#### `common/models/extendedmodels/ExtendedCommittee.php`
**Enhanced duplicate checking:**
```php
public function checkMemberAvailbaleInCommittee($committeePeriodId, $designationId, 
    $memberId, $committeeGroupId, $isSpouse = 0, $dependantId = null)
```
- Checks `dependantid` for dependants
- Checks `isspouse + NULL dependantid` for member/spouse
- Allows same member as member, spouse, and multiple dependants

**Enhanced save method:**
```php
public function saveCommitteeMember($designationId, $memberId, $committeeGroupId, 
    $committeePeriodId, $institutionid, $dependantId = null)
```
- Accepts optional `dependantId` parameter
- Sets `isspouse = 0` for dependants

#### `common/models/extendedmodels/ExtendedCommitteePeriod.php`
**Replaced stored procedure with direct SQL query (280+ lines):**
- Complex CASE statements for name, title, image, phone, email
- **Relation inference logic** (18 mapping rules):
  - Son → Daughter-in-law
  - Daughter → Son-in-law
  - Father → Mother
  - Mother → Father
  - Brother → Sister-in-law
  - Sister → Brother-in-law
  - And 12 more mappings
- **Remarks field** format: `"[relation] of [parent title] [parent name]"`
  - Example: "Son of Mr. John Smith"
- Proper name concatenation using `CONCAT_WS` with `NULLIF` (prevents double spaces)
- LEFT JOIN with partner dependant for relation inference

### 2. Controllers Updated

#### `backend/controllers/CommitteeController.php`
**Three new actions added:**

1. **`actionGetMemberDependants()`**
   - Loads all dependants for a selected member
   - Returns with relation inference logic
   - Used for automatic dependant display

2. **`actionGetDependantDetails()`**
   - Retrieves full dependant information
   - Includes parent member details
   - Applies relation inference

3. **`actionGetDependantForSearch()`**
   - Search dependants by name
   - Returns matching dependants with parent info

**Updated existing action:**
- `actionSaveCommitteeMember()` - Now passes `isSpouse` and `dependantId` to duplicate check

#### `api/modules/v3/controllers/CommitteeController.php`
**API response enhanced with:**
- `dependantId`: Numeric ID or null
- `isDependant`: Boolean flag (`dependantid IS NOT NULL`)
- `relation`: Inferred relation (e.g., "Son", "Daughter-in-law")
- `remarks`: Contextual string (e.g., "Son of Mr. John Smith")

### 3. Views Updated

#### `backend/views/committee/index.php`
- Hidden separate "Add Dependants" tab (simplified UI per user feedback)

#### `backend/views/committee/_members.php`
- Added `MemberDependantsSection` div for dependant cards
- Added `CommitteeAssignmentSection` for assignment form

#### `backend/views/committee/_addmember.php`
**Major enhancements:**
- Dependants display section (auto-shows when member has dependants)
- Individual dependant cards with "Add to Committee" buttons
- Hidden fields for dependant selection:
  - `selected-dependant-id`
  - `is-dependant-selected`
- Dynamic section header changes based on selection
- CSS for `.selected-dependant` class (green highlight)
- Shows relation under dependant name

#### `backend/views/committee/_committeemembers.php`
**Display changes:**
- Shows `remarks` field instead of `relation` field
- Format: "Son of Mr. John Smith" (more contextual than just "Son")

#### `backend/views/committee/_adddependant.php`
- Separate dependant search interface (kept for alternative workflow)
- Displays dependant details with parent member info

### 4. JavaScript Updates

#### `backend/assets/theme/js/Remember.committeeAddMember.ui.js`
**New functionality:**

1. **`_loadMemberDependants(memberId)`**
   - AJAX call to load member's dependants
   - Builds visual cards for each dependant
   - Shows relation, image, mobile
   - Displays "Add to Committee" buttons

2. **Dependant selection handler** (`.select-dependant-for-committee`)
   - Visual feedback with green highlighting
   - Updates hidden fields
   - Changes section header to "Assigning Dependant to Committee"
   - Shows parent member context

3. **Clear selection handler** (`.clear-dependant-selection`)
   - Resets to member mode
   - Removes highlighting
   - Clears hidden fields

4. **Enhanced save handler**
   - Includes `dependantId` in POST data
   - Passes to save action

### 5. Configuration Updates

#### `backend/config/params.php`
**Added URL routes:**
```php
'getMemberDependants' => '/committee/get-member-dependants',
'getDependantDetails' => '/committee/get-dependant-details',
'getDependantForSearch' => '/committee/get-dependant-for-search',
```

## Technical Implementation Details

### Relation Inference Logic
When a dependant's relation is empty, the system infers it from their partner's relation:

```sql
CASE 
    WHEN dep.relation IS NOT NULL AND dep.relation != '' THEN dep.relation
    WHEN partner.relation = 'Son' THEN 'Daughter-in-law'
    WHEN partner.relation = 'Daughter' THEN 'Son-in-law'
    -- ... 16 more mappings
    WHEN dep.dependantid IS NOT NULL THEN 'Spouse'
    ELSE ''
END
```

### Duplicate Prevention Strategy
The system checks the combination of three fields:
- For dependants: `memberid + dependantid + designationid + committeegroupid`
- For member/spouse: `memberid + isspouse + (dependantid IS NULL)`

This allows:
- John Smith as committee member
- John Smith's spouse as committee member
- John Smith's son as committee member
- John Smith's daughter as committee member
- All with different or same designations

### Name Concatenation Fix
Changed from:
```sql
CONCAT(COALESCE(firstName, ''), ' ', COALESCE(middleName, ''), ' ', COALESCE(lastName, ''))
```

To:
```sql
TRIM(CONCAT_WS(' ', NULLIF(firstName, ''), NULLIF(middleName, ''), NULLIF(lastName, '')))
```

**Benefits:**
- Eliminates double spaces when middle name is empty
- No leading/trailing spaces
- Cleaner data output

## User Workflow

### Adding a Dependant to Committee

1. Navigate to Committee Management

## Documentation fixes

- **Add `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` and `SENTRY_TOKEN` to `configuration.md`** — primary CI/CD auth variables were missing from the env vars reference
- **Add `SENTRY_INSTALL_DIR` and `SENTRY_NO_CACHE` to `configuration.md`** — undocumented env vars

- **Expand README commands table** from 6 to 14 entries

## Embed skill files at build time

Previously, `sentry cli setup` fetched skill files from GitHub at runtime — fetching content that was generated from the CLI's own source code. This was a roundtrip: the CLI generates skill files from Stricli introspection, they live in the repo, and then the CLI fetches them back from GitHub by URL, using a hardcoded `REFERENCE_FILES` array that required codegen to keep in sync.

Now:
- `generate-skill.ts` produces `src/generated/skill-content.ts` that inlines all skill file contents (~47KB) as a `Map<string, string>`
- `agent-skills.ts` imports the embedded content and writes it directly to `~/.claude/skills/` — no network fetch, no URL construction, no version-pinning logic
- `REFERENCE_FILES` array, `getSkillUrl()`, `fetchSingleFile()`, `fetchAllSkillFiles()`, `fetchSkillContent()` — all removed
- `generate:skill` is chained before `build`/`dev`/`typecheck`/`test` in `package.json` (like `generate:sdk`)

body:
## Summary
This PR significantly refactors the `NegativeEdgeSampler` class to remove Intel TBB dependencies, simplify the public API, and introduce explicit temporal batch processing. The new design separates concerns between batch ingestion and negative sampling, making the code more maintainable and easier to reason about.

## Key Changes

- **Removed TBB dependencies**: Eliminated `tbb::concurrent_unordered_set`, `tbb::concurrent_unordered_map`, and `tbb::concurrent_vector`. The class now uses standard containers (`std::vector`) with a cleaner, single-threaded design.

- **Simplified public API**: 
  - Replaced the complex `sample_negative_edges_per_batch()` method with a two-step process: `add_batch()` followed by `sample_negatives()`
  - Removed the standalone `collect_all_negatives_by_timestamp()` function
  - Constructor now takes configuration parameters directly (is_directed, num_negatives_per_positive, historical_negative_percentage, seed)

- **Introduced temporal batch processing**:
  - `add_batch()` ingests positive edges with timestamps for a single batch
  - `sample_negatives()` samples negatives for the most recently added batch
  - Batches are processed in temporal order, with history accumulated across batches

- **Improved internal state management**:
  - `all_nodes_sorted_`: Maintains a sorted, deduplicated list of all nodes seen
  - `history_neighbors_`: Cumulative adjacency from all previous batches
  - `batch_neighbors_`: Adjacency for the current batch only
  - Clear separation between historical and current batch state

- **Enhanced sampling logic**:
  - `sample_random_negatives()`: Uses skip-over technique to efficiently sample from non-neighbors
  - `sample_historical_negatives()`: Samples from edges in history but not in current batch
  - `NegativeSampleResult` struct: Returns both sources/targets and actual counts of sampled negatives

- **Added utility methods**:
  - `node_index()`: Binary search for node position
  - `merge_new_nodes()`: Handles node list updates
  - `build_batch_neighbors()`: Constructs adjacency for current batch
  - `update_history()`: Merges batch edges into historical state
  - Getters for node count, edge count, and batch count

## Implementation Details

- Removed debug mode infrastructure (`is_debug_enabled()`, `PairHash`)
- Switched to standard C++ random number generation (`std::mt19937`)
- All node lists are maintained in sorted order for efficient binary search and deduplication
- The skip-over algorithm avoids materializing the full complement set when sampling random negatives
- Temporal ordering is enforced at the caller level (not validated internally)

## 1) Struttura repo (alto livello) — OK per Next.js
A livello root hai cartelle/file tipici di un progetto **Next.js + Prisma**:
- `app/` (App Router)
- `components/`, `lib/`, `prisma/`, `public/`

Dentro `app/` risulta anche una sottocartella **`app/app`**.

- route duplicate/confuse
- layout/page non presi come ti aspetti
- build più “strana” o conflitti di routing

author: git-on-my-level
body:
## What changed
The web UI now treats refresh-token rotation failures as retryable auth-session rehydration races instead of immediately collapsing the browser into a logged-out state.

The patch does three things:
- classifies `invalid_token` refresh failures during session rehydration as retryable rather than final logout
- keeps proxy refresh handling from clearing the workspace session on those retryable failures
- retries `/auth/session` rehydration once on the client before clearing the in-memory authenticated agent

## Root cause
The previous fix only recognized a stale rotated refresh token if a short-lived access-token cookie was still present.

Once that access cookie aged out, the same refresh-rotation race was misclassified as a hard auth failure. In practice that meant a page load or proxied request that arrived after another request had already rotated the refresh token could flip the UI back to the login flow even though the 30-day refresh session was still valid.

## Impact
Self-hosted passkey sessions should no longer appear to log out early just because the browser hit a stale rotated refresh token after the access cookie expired.

## Validation
- `make -C web-ui check`

## Summary

This PR adds the first version of the trip resource assignment search flow in `miot-cli`.

It introduces new APIs to:
- search available carrier candidates for a trip assignment
- search driver, truck, and trailer candidates for a selected carrier

The response is enriched with operational data from external sources, including:
- accreditation status from Coordinator
- live assignment status from StreamHub
- KPI summary data for drivers, trucks, and trailers

It also includes identifier normalization fixes so KPI summaries are correctly attached even when StreamHub values use different raw formats.

## What Changed

### New Trip Assignment APIs
- Added `POST /api/v1/trip-resource-assignments/carriers/search`
- Added `POST /api/v1/trip-resource-assignments/resources/search`

### Carrier Search
- Returns active carriers for the current tenant
- Includes calculated carrier fields such as:
  - driver counts
  - blocked / occasional driver counts
  - transport license presence and expiration info

### Resource Search
- Validates the selected carrier belongs to the current tenant
- Loads carrier resources:
  - drivers
  - trucks
  - trailers
- Enriches each candidate with:
  - accreditation state
  - live trip assignment data
  - KPI summary fields

### External Data Integration
- Added configurable access to:
  - Coordinator datasource
  - StreamHub datasource
- Added reactive datasource resolution for external lookups
- Added assignment-specific configuration for schemas and datasource toggles

### KPI Enrichment
- Added support for:
  - `driver_kpi_summary`
  - `truck_kpi_summary`
  - `trailer_kpi_summary`
- Exposes KPI fields in `calculatedFields`, such as:
  - `previousTrips`
  - `lastTripId`
  - `lastTripStartTime`
  - `lastTripEndTime`
  - `traveledKilometers`
  - `speedLimitEvents`
  - `continuousRestingEvents`
  - `lostSignalEvents`

### Identifier Normalization Fixes
- Normalized KPI lookups for:
  - drivers by `rut`
  - trucks by `externalId` and `licensePlate`
  - trailers by `licensePlate`
- This fixes cases where KPI data existed in StreamHub but was not being attached to API results because of formatting differences between raw and normalized identifiers

### Misc
- Enabled `Flyway` out-of-order execution in the CLI migrator
- Added application properties needed for the new external assignment integrations

## Validation

Validated locally with:
- `./mvnw -pl miot-cli -DskipTests compile`

## Notes

This PR focuses on candidate discovery and enrichment for trip assignment.  
The request contracts already include booking/slot context, while the current implementation centers on tenant, carrier, accreditation, live assignment, and KPI-based enrichment.

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce PR noise and review overhead by consolidating dependency updates into fewer, larger PRs scoped by ecosystem area.
- Bias Dependabot toward area-level batching (Cargo, third_party, GitHub Actions, Docker/devcontainer) instead of many single-version PRs.
- Mirror the requested consolidation pattern used for related projects so maintainers receive coordinated update bundles.

### Description
- Updated `/.github/dependabot.yml` to explicitly prefer fewer, larger, area-grouped PRs and adjusted the top-level rationale comments to reflect this strategy.
- Set `open-pull-requests-limit: 2` for the configured ecosystems (root Cargo, `third_party/rmp`, `github-actions`, Docker main, and `/.devcontainer`) to bias Dependabot toward consolidated update batches.
- Broadened `groups` so each area groups `major`, `minor`, and `patch` updates (added area groups like `cargo-root-updates`, `rmp-ecosystem`, `github-actions-updates`, `docker-main-updates`, and `devcontainer-updates`) and removed the previous per-crate exclusion rules that split core crates into separate streams.
- Replaced all stale relative PR-limit section comments ("Higher PR limit", "Moderate PR limit", "Lower PR limit") with neutral, factual language (`Consolidated PR limit: <rationale>`) to eliminate comment/config drift.
- Added `scripts/check-dependabot-config.sh` — a validation script that catches three categories of comment/config drift: relative PR-limit terminology, missing `open-pull-requests-limit` fields, and inline numeric comment values that don't match the configured limit.
- Integrated the validation script into the pre-commit hook (Check 23, triggered when `dependabot.yml` is staged) and into the `yaml-lint` CI workflow as a semantic validation step.
- Added `.llm/skills/ci-cd-troubleshooting-example-dependabot-comment-drift.md` documenting the root cause, fix, and prevention infrastructure for this class of issue.

### Testing
- Parsed `/.github/dependabot.yml` with a Ruby YAML loader (`ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file(".github/dependabot.yml")'`) and the file parsed successfully.
- Ran a targeted Python content check to verify broad grouping and that `open-pull-requests-limit: 2` is applied to all configured ecosystems, and those checks passed.
- Verified `scripts/check-dependabot-config.sh` passes cleanly against the updated config and correctly catches all three error categories (relative terminology, missing limit, numeric mismatch) against a synthetic bad config.
- Confirmed YAML syntax validity with `yamllint` on all changed `.yml` files.
- Attempted to fetch the reference config at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ambiguous-Interactive/signal-fish-cloud/main/.github/dependabot.yml` for direct comparison, but the request returned HTTP 403 so direct upstream comparison could not be completed in this environment.

1. In case of chrome error during termination (`stop`), those errors can not be in the log, since the log was already saved.
2. Chrome buffers logs a lot more than anticipated, and because `--v=0` logs are a lot less chatty than `--v=1` the logs routinely show essentially nothing (a few tour steps are logged then nothing).

Also make `stop` a bit more resilient to chrome issues:

- handle errors around ws shutdown
- wait for chrome to shut down before we try to remove the data directory

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce Dependabot churn by preferring fewer, larger, ecosystem-grouped PRs that batch many version updates together.
- Make Cargo and GitHub Actions updates appear as consolidated, reviewable batches rather than many single-package PRs.
- Align the repository's Dependabot behavior with the requested high-consolidation strategy used elsewhere in the org.

### Description
- Rewrote `.github/dependabot.yml` to create a single Cargo group `cargo-all-dependencies` with `patterns: ["*"]` and `update-types` set to `major`, `minor`, and `patch`.
- Added a single GitHub Actions group `github-actions-all` with `patterns: ["*"]` and `update-types` set to `major`, `minor`, and `patch`.
- Set `open-pull-requests-limit: 1` for both ecosystems so Dependabot can only open one consolidated batch PR at a time; once merged, a fresh batch is opened for any remaining pending updates.
- Updated header comment from "area PRs" to "ecosystem-based PRs" to accurately describe the grouping strategy.
- Updated inline comments to precisely match the enforced single-PR behavior.
- Added three structural policy tests in `tests/ci_config_tests.rs` (`dependency_policy` module) to prevent future comment/value drift:
  - `dependabot_each_ecosystem_sets_open_prs_limit_to_one` — every ecosystem block must set the limit to exactly `1`.
  - `dependabot_open_prs_limits_are_all_consistent` — all `open-pull-requests-limit` values must be identical across ecosystems.
  - `dependabot_each_ecosystem_has_wildcard_catchall_group` — every ecosystem must declare a `- "*"` catchall pattern.
- Updated `.llm/skills/ci-configuration.md` with a note documenting the Dependabot comment/value consistency rule and pointing at the enforcement tests.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo fmt` and it completed successfully.
- Ran `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and it completed successfully with no warnings.
- Ran `cargo test --all-features --test ci_config_tests` which produced `165 passed; 0 failed`, including all three new Dependabot policy tests.
- Validated the YAML structure of `.github/dependabot.yml` with `ruby -ryaml` which succeeded.
